analysis.title: S&P 500 Futures: Into and (Temporarily?) Out of the Correction
key_insights: Non-Dealers bought $19.1bn of S&P 500 futures in the Nov 10-17 COT window, the 6th straight week of net buying, for a cumulative $71.3bn since Oct 6. New longs ($24.6bn) outweighed new shorts ($5.5bn) while the S&P fell 2.4%.

Hedge Funds bought $25.5bn, 71% of it gross long additions. Some of this may be offsets to single stock shorts or put positions, as S&P 3 month implied vol and normalized 25 delta put-call skew both richened.

Asset Manager short selling of $9.4bn was the largest since July 2025, which suggests sensitivity to an AI and growth slowdown. AI Semiconductors fell 4.8% and High Beta Cyclicals fell 5.2% in the window.
Short-term correlations between Asset Manager shorts and AI semis and high beta cyclicals became more negative.
From Nov 17 to Nov 20 the S&P plunged 5.9% and funding cheapened. E-Mini aggregate open interest rose $36.6bn, with $26.6bn on Nov 20, the biggest 1 day change in 2026 excluding roll periods.
The Nov 23 rebound, sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement, produced only a modest $7.9bn OI retracement. Either significant long buying occurred or some bears held.
risk_factors: AI and growth slowdown sensitivity among Asset Managers.
Broadening S&P short selling and rising OI after the Nov 20 close.
Rebound on Nov 23 may be fragile if bears held positions.
